toolchainRemediation.problem: Both node_modules paths in the producer worktree were NTFS junctions into the quarantined dirty repo. Any install, test or build command could therefore write into a read-only quarantine, and no verification result from that worktree could be trusted.
toolchainRemediation.resolution: Junctions removed link-only via cmd rmdir, never Remove-Item -Recurse, so the junction targets were not followed and the quarantine's node_modules survived intact. A real dependency tree was installed from an isolated store on the same volume as the worktree, so pnpm hardlinks rather than copies.
toolchainRemediation.redirection: Environment variables only — npm_config_store_dir, npm_config_cache, npm_config_tmp. The repo's .npmrc is git-tracked and carries the GitHub Packages registry line, so editing it would have dirtied the worktree and broken the clean-tree acceptance condition. It was left untouched.
toolchainRemediation.electronNote: Install ran with --ignore-scripts, so Electron's postinstall was skipped and the binary was missing. Resolved by copying the already-present electron-v34.5.8-win32-x64.zip into the isolated cache and running Electron's own install.js offline. No network fetch, and no other package's lifecycle script was executed.
toolchainRemediation.noWriteProof: Dirty repo git status hash, HEAD, line count and both node_modules mtimes are byte-identical before and after a full install plus typecheck plus 946-test run.
toolchainRemediation.measurementCorrection: An intermediate no-write comparison appeared to fail. Cause was the measurement, not the tree: sorting the status lines before hashing produced 9EC81452..., while natural git order produced B4850D68... which matches the baseline. Line-by-line diff of two snapshots taken 41 seconds apart returned zero differing lines. Recorded because a coordinator artifact must not hide a check that first read as a failure.

hashPolicy: Hashes are measured on working-tree bytes at the accepted commits. .gitattributes may normalise line endings on a fresh checkout, which changes file bytes and therefore hashes — compare working-tree to working-tree, never working-tree to a fresh clone. If a hash disagrees, re-hash from the ref before treating it as tampering.
